facts.text: On this day in 1517, Martin Luther nailed his 95 Theses to a church door in Wittenberg — an act of academic protest that accidentally fractured Western Christianity for centuries.
Halloween is older than the United States. The Celtic festival Samhain, its direct ancestor, has been observed on October 31 for over 2,000 years.
More people live inside a circle drawn around Dhaka, Bangladesh than in the entire United States west of the Mississippi River.
Norway owns an uninhabited island called Bouvet Island — the most remote piece of land on Earth, 1,700 miles from the nearest inhabited place — and almost never visits it.
The city of Istanbul sits in two countries simultaneously. Its western districts are geographically in Europe; its eastern districts are in Asia, separated by the Bosphorus Strait.
On Oct 31, 1929, the Dow posted its biggest single-day gain of the entire crash era — up 12.3% — just two days after Black Tuesday. Panic and euphoria were always neighbors.
On Oct 31, 2008, Satoshi Nakamoto published the Bitcoin white paper. The system designed to replace banks was born on Halloween.
The NYSE's famously loud closing bell was originally a Chinese gong. It wasn't replaced with an actual bell until 1903.
Saudi Aramco briefly surpassed $2 trillion in market cap in 2022 — making it worth more than the entire GDP of Italy.
Short sellers collectively lost over $300 billion in January 2021 during the GameStop squeeze. It remains the costliest month for short positions in Wall Street history.
On this date in 1961, the Soviet Union detonated Tsar Bomba — a 50-megaton hydrogen bomb so powerful its fireball nearly reached the altitude of the plane that dropped it.
On Halloween 1517, Luther nailed his theses to the church door. Less noted: the oak wood he used is still standing inside Wittenberg's Castle Church.
Your skeleton is not static. Every 10 years, your body has replaced roughly 100% of its bone mass — you are, structurally, a different person than you were a decade ago.
A neutron star packs more mass than the Sun into a sphere the size of a city. A single teaspoon of its material would weigh approximately 10 million tons on Earth.
Octopuses have three hearts, blue copper-based blood, and neurons distributed so heavily through their arms that each limb can taste, feel, and make decisions independently of the brain.
On this day in 1517, Luther nailed his 95 Theses to the Wittenberg church door — sparking the Reformation. The modern nation of Germany is younger than the schism Luther caused within Christianity.
Oxford University was teaching students when the Aztec Empire didn't yet exist. Oxford dates to 1096; the Aztecs founded Tenochtitlan in 1325.
On this day in 1941, Mount Rushmore was declared complete after 14 years of carving. The sculpture is younger than commercial air travel.
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the construction of the Great Pyramid. She died in 30 BC; the pyramids rose around 2560 BC.
The fax machine was patented in 1843 — before the American Civil War. When Sherman marched to the sea, fax technology already existed.
Sonder (n.): the realization that each passerby has a life as vivid and complex as your own. Coined by John Koenig in The Dictionary of Obscure Sorrows, 2012. Already feels ancient.
Mamihlapinatapai: a Yaghan word for the look shared by two people who both want something but neither will initiate. Linguists cite it as one of the most succinct words ever recorded.
On this day in 1517, Luther nailed his theses to a church door — and the word 'Protestant' entered history within a decade, derived from the Latin protestari: to bear witness publicly.
Vellichor (n.): the strange wistfulness of a used bookshop. Like sonder, it comes from Koenig — proof that naming a feeling is often the same as inventing it.
On this day in 1926, Houdini died. His name is now a verb: to houdini means to escape from a seemingly impossible situation. It appears in dictionaries, quietly, without fanfare.
On Oct 31, 2008, Satoshi Nakamoto published the Bitcoin whitepaper to a cryptography mailing list. Nine people received it. None replied with enthusiasm.
On Oct 31, 2013, the first Bitcoin ATM went live in a Vancouver coffee shop, charging a 3% fee. It processed $10,000 in transactions on day one.
Ethereum's gas limit is set by miners — not the protocol. Every block, validators vote to nudge it up or down by 0.1%, making throughput a rolling consensus rather than a hard rule.
The 2016 DAO hack didn't break Ethereum's code. The attacker exploited a reentrancy bug in a third-party contract, then legally argued the funds were theirs by the protocol's own rules.
Bitcoin's timelock opcode, CHECKLOCKTIMEVERIFY, sat dormant in the codebase for years before activation. Satoshi included it in the original release, apparently without documentation or announcement.

On this date in 2011, Apple released Siri — the first mainstream LLM-adjacent assistant. It ran almost entirely on-device NLP rules, not neural nets. The transformer architecture that would replace it didn't exist yet.
On this date in 1998, Yann LeCun's team at Bell Labs published the MNIST benchmark paper. It remained the default sanity-check dataset for neural networks for over two decades.
GPT-4's training run is estimated to have consumed roughly 50 gigawatt-hours of electricity — comparable to the annual consumption of 4,500 average US homes, spent in weeks.

AlphaFold 2 predicted structures for over 200 million proteins before most structural biologists had time to review the first batch. It effectively rendered a 50-year grand challenge tractable in one release.

The first neural network to beat humans at Go, AlphaGo, defeated Fan Hui in October 2015 — but DeepMind kept it secret for months. The world learned about it only when the Nature paper dropped in January 2016.
